correctness.rationale: The Dirichlet Green kernel is explicit, continuous, zero at endpoints, and has unit derivative jump; distributional measure representation gives each cell error. Its sup equals 0.5*tan(h/2); direct integration yields cos(t-h/2)/cos(h/2)-1 with maximum sec(h/2)-1. The pi-periodic curvature measure gives each antipodal paired open interval equal variation and at most M/2, producing the global 0.25*tan(h*/2) factor. The rank-one seminorm |<v,x>| has exactly two interior curvature atoms of weight 2, M=4, so both ratios attain the claimed constants. Sum of half-circle gaps pi and strict monotonicity prove minimax uniqueness. A 372-case finite checker passed; no infinite result is inferred from tests.

originality.rationale: The closest original full text, Unser 2026 Proposition 5.2, proves the uniform-grid curvature-variation bounds and uses the same Green kernel, but its full-circle L1 estimate is the larger 0.5*h*tan(h/2); it does not give the exact L1 coefficient sec(h/2)-1, the global symmetric normalized Linfty constant 0.25*tan(h*/2) on arbitrary nonuniform antipodal fans, simultaneous rank-one-seminorm equality, or the unique minimax fan. The earlier generalized-TV representer theorem solves a different inverse problem. Actual semantic database searches and accessible historical claims found no implication covering this full claim. Older general spline literature leaves an explicit priority risk; those abstract-only works are not labeled decisively noncovering.
residual_risks: Exact interval Green operator norms may already be implicit or explicit in classical trigonometric, Chebyshevian or L-spline texts; historical full texts of Schoenberg (1964) and Koch (1984) were not reviewed.

There is a possibility that a general theorem about worst-case interpolation of periodic functions under second-order variation constraints implies the formulas, even without mentioning conic splines.
The authors of the 2026 motivating paper might subsequently publish refined constants; earliest public source date and comparison refer to the specified v1.

value.rationale: A natural recent quasi-norm/conic-spline approximation question calls for exact cost of a finite number of sampling rays under Hessian/curvature variation. The result computes both sharp whole-circle errors for EVERY nonuniform centrally symmetric fan, gives a single geometric seminorm saturating both, and determines the unique minimax angular placement. On uniform grids the L1 constant is asymptotically half the published coefficient, which is meaningful for quantitative regularizer discretization. These are natural complete operator constants, not an artificial numerical slice; higher-dimensional analogues remain open.
